column2: Which environment does get_exec_path consult when no env mapping is supplied?
column3: It uses os.environ.

column2: What must the first argument of os.fdopen be, unlike the first argument of open?
column3: An integer file descriptor.

column2: On macOS and FreeBSD, when does sendfile write its headers and trailers?
column3: Before and after the data read from in_fd.

column2: When does os.mknod use its device argument?
column3: For character or block device nodes; otherwise it is ignored.

column2: When is a scandir iterator closed automatically?
column3: On exhaustion, garbage collection, or an error during iteration.

column2: Can os.stat take an open file descriptor instead of a pathname?
column3: Yes; it accepts an open file descriptor as well as string, bytes, and PathLike paths.

column2: How can code check whether a particular OS function accepts a file descriptor as its path?
column3: Test membership of the function in os.supports_fd.

column2: Is a new descriptor returned by os.eventfd inheritable by default?
column3: No, it is non-inheritable by default.

column2: How do the l and v variants of exec functions receive command-line arguments?
column3: The l variants take separate arguments; v variants take a list or tuple.

column2: What signal mask does a posix_spawn child inherit when setsigmask is omitted?
column3: The parent's signal mask.

column2: Do replacements of sys.stdin affect the subprocess launched by os.system?
column3: No; such changes are not reflected in the executed command's environment.

column2: May waitstatus_to_exitcode be called when WIFSTOPPED(status) is true?
column3: No; the caller must check for that condition first.

column2: How does ChainMap.new_child isolate updates from parent mappings?
column3: It puts a new mapping first while retaining the current mappings behind it.

column2: Are zero and negative values allowed as Counter counts?
column3: Yes; counts may be any integer, including zero or negative.

column2: Does Counter.subtract replace existing counts or subtract from them?
column3: It subtracts counts; both inputs and outputs can be zero or negative.

column2: Do Counter multiset operations retain zero and negative results?
column3: No; only positive results are emitted.

column2: What happens to input order when deque.extendleft adds an iterable?
column3: The repeated left appends reverse its order.

column2: How can deque.rotate help implement slicing?
column3: Rotate the target to the left, remove and add entries, then reverse the rotation.

column2: How is defaultdict.default_factory called for a missing key?
column3: Without arguments; the result is inserted for the key and returned.

column2: What string formats can specify namedtuple field names?
column3: Names separated by whitespace, commas, or both.

column2: Which namedtuple parameters receive defaults when only some defaults are supplied?
column3: The rightmost parameters.

column2: Since which Python version is insertion order guaranteed for ordinary dictionaries?
column3: Python 3.7.

column2: Where does UserDict expose the regular dictionary holding its contents?
column3: In its data attribute.

column2: Does UserList keep the supplied iterable itself as its initial contents?
column3: It initializes its data with a copy, defaulting to an empty list.

column2: Which function should accumulate use to compute a running product?
column3: operator.mul.

column2: Does itertools.batched consume the entire input before yielding a batch?
column3: No; it consumes only enough to fill a batch and yields lazily.

column2: When does itertools.compress stop if its two inputs have different lengths?
column3: When either data or selectors is exhausted.

column2: How are the values produced by itertools.count spaced?
column3: They are evenly spaced by step, beginning at start.

column2: What does filterfalse retain when its predicate argument is None?
column3: Items whose own truth value is false.

column2: Why can itertools.groupby split equal keys into separate groups?
column3: It starts a new group whenever the key changes, unlike SQL aggregation.

column2: What does pairwise produce for an input with fewer than two values?
column3: An empty iterator.

column2: How many permutations of length r are produced when r exceeds the number of inputs?
column3: Zero.

column2: Which input position advances fastest in itertools.product?
column3: The rightmost position.

column2: Can the first element failing takewhile's predicate be recovered from the remaining input?
column3: No; takewhile has already consumed it.

column2: When can list be faster than tee for splitting an iterator?
column3: When one consumer uses most or all values before another begins.

column2: How do the itertools recipes avoid bringing an entire iterable into memory?
column3: They process elements one at a time.

column2: How should a file passed to csv.reader be opened to let the CSV module handle newlines?
column3: With newline=''.

column2: Which takes precedence when register_dialect receives both a dialect and formatting keywords?
column3: The formatting keywords override the dialect parameters.

column2: Does DictReader include the first input row when fieldnames are explicitly provided?
column3: Yes; otherwise the first row supplies names and is omitted from results.

column2: What happens by default when DictWriter receives a key absent from fieldnames?
column3: It raises ValueError; extrasaction='ignore' skips extra keys.

column2: What quoting policy is used by csv.unix_dialect?
column3: All fields are quoted, with a newline line terminator.

column2: How does Sniffer choose between delimiters that fit a sample equally well?
column3: By their order in the preferred attribute, regardless of frequency.

column2: Under QUOTE_MINIMAL, what kinds of fields are quoted?
column3: Fields containing special delimiter, quote, or line-ending characters.

column2: Why are bool, Fraction, and IntEnum problematic in QUOTE_NONNUMERIC reader mode?
column3: Their string representations cannot be converted to float.

column2: How does QUOTE_NOTNULL serialize None?
column3: As an empty unquoted string; other fields are quoted.

column2: What is the default CSV quote character?
column3: A double quote.

column2: What does DictWriter.writeheader write?
column3: A row of the constructor's field names, formatted with the current dialect.

column2: What writing problem can occur on CRLF platforms when newline='' is omitted?
column3: An extra carriage return can be added.

column2: Can the default JSON serializer output also be used as YAML?
column3: Yes; it is a subset of YAML 1.2 and, with default separators, YAML 1.0 and 1.1.

column2: What does json.dump do with non-basic dictionary keys when skipkeys is true?
column3: It skips them instead of raising TypeError.

column2: What happens when allow_nan is false and a non-finite float is serialized?
column3: A ValueError is raised.

column2: What must the default callback for an otherwise unserializable object return?
column3: A JSON-encodable version, or it must raise TypeError.

column2: How is the return value of object_hook used during JSON decoding?
column3: It replaces the decoded dictionary.

column2: What argument is passed to the parse_int callback?
column3: The string representation of each JSON integer.

column2: Which input types can json.loads deserialize?
column3: A str, bytes, or bytearray containing a JSON document.

column2: What two values does JSONDecoder.raw_decode return?
column3: The Python representation and the position where the JSON document ended.

column2: Does ensure_ascii=False permit unescaped control characters in JSON output?
column3: No; quotation marks, backslashes, and required control characters remain escaped.

column2: Why might sort_keys be useful in JSON regression tests?
column3: Sorting keys makes serialized dictionaries easier to compare consistently.

column2: How does the JSON deserializer react to an initial byte order mark?
column3: It raises ValueError.

column2: Which value is retained for a repeated name in a decoded JSON object?
column3: The last name-value pair.

column2: Which module should be used when mathematical functions need complex-number support?
column3: cmath.

column2: Does math.isqrt round the exact square root up or down?
column3: Down, to the greatest integer whose square does not exceed n.

column2: What does math.lcm return when called with no arguments?
column3: One.

column2: Which special method handles math.floor for a non-float object?
column3: __floor__, which should return an Integral value.

column2: How does Python's math.modf return its two results?
column3: As a pair, rather than through a C-style output parameter.

column2: What sign does a zero result from math.remainder have?
column3: The sign of x.

column2: Why do sufficiently large Python floats have no fractional bits?
column3: Their finite precision makes all values of that magnitude exact integers.

column2: Which magnitude determines the relative tolerance used by math.isclose?
column3: The larger absolute value of the two operands.

column2: Does math.isclose consider NaN close to itself?
column3: No.

column2: Why is expm1 preferable to exp(x)-1 for small x?
column3: It avoids the significant precision loss from the subtraction.

column2: Why is erfc useful for large arguments?
column3: It avoids loss of significance from subtracting erf(x) from one.

column2: How should code check whether a value is NaN?
column3: Use isnan instead of identity or equality comparisons.

column2: Which measure of central tendency is suggested when outliers make the mean unrepresentative?
column3: The median.

column2: Can fmean assign unequal weights to observations?
column3: Yes; it supports optional weights.

column2: Does the rectangular KDE kernel give weight to points outside its bandwidth?
column3: No; it only weights points within the bandwidth.

column2: What happens when median receives an empty iterable?
column3: It raises StatisticsError.

column2: What distribution within an age bin does the grouped-median example assume?
column3: An even distribution across the interval.

column2: When several modes have equal frequency, which one does mode return?
column3: The first encountered in the data.

column2: What does pvariance calculate when mu is omitted?
column3: It automatically calculates and uses the arithmetic mean.

column2: What is the minimum number of observations required by variance?
column3: Two real-valued observations.

column2: Can quantiles operate without any data points?
column3: No; it raises StatisticsError.

column2: How does the inclusive quantile method treat the minimum and maximum observations?
column3: As the zeroth and hundredth percentiles.

column2: What probability does NormalDist.cdf(x) calculate?
column3: The probability that the random variable is less than or equal to x.

column2: Can independent normally distributed variables be added using NormalDist objects?
column3: Yes; addition and subtraction of independent normal variables are supported.

column2: What does current_thread return for a thread created outside the threading module?
column3: A dummy thread object with limited functionality.

column2: Does threading.enumerate include the main thread after it has terminated?
column3: Yes; the main thread remains included.

column2: Which Thread methods should a subclass override to define its activity?
column3: Only __init__ and run.

column2: What is Thread.native_id before the thread starts?
column3: None.

column2: What does a nonblocking Lock.acquire return when the lock cannot be acquired immediately?
column3: False.

column2: How many releases must match repeated acquisitions of an RLock?
column3: One release for every acquisition, by the acquiring thread.

column2: Can several Condition objects share the same lock?
column3: Yes; pass the same lock to them.

column2: Why must an application recheck its condition after a Condition.wait returns?
column3: The condition that prompted notification may no longer hold.

column2: What argument does Condition.wait_for repeatedly evaluate?
column3: A callable predicate interpreted as a boolean.

column2: What happens when Semaphore.acquire finds its counter at zero?
column3: It blocks until another thread releases the semaphore.

column2: What does Event.wait return when its timeout expires without the flag being set?
column3: False.

column2: What do lock-like context managers call when entering and leaving a with block?
column3: acquire on entry and release on exit.

column2: What common interface is implemented by the thread and process pool executors?
column3: The abstract Executor interface.

column2: From which moment is an Executor.map timeout measured?
column3: From the original call to Executor.map.

column2: What happens when submit is called after an executor has shut down?
column3: It raises RuntimeError.

column2: Does shutdown(cancel_futures=True) cancel futures that are already running?
column3: No; it only cancels pending futures that have not started.

column2: Does leaving an executor's with block wait for its work to finish?
column3: Yes; shutdown behaves as if wait=True.

column2: What happens to pending jobs when a ThreadPoolExecutor initializer raises an exception?
column3: They raise BrokenThreadPool, as do subsequent submissions.

column2: Should a lambda defined in a REPL be expected to work with ProcessPoolExecutor?
column3: No; pickling restrictions apply.

column2: Which exception follows failure of a ProcessPoolExecutor initializer?
column3: BrokenProcessPool.

column2: What should a multithreaded POSIX application change when fork-based process-pool creation raises a warning?
column3: Use an mp_context configured with a different start method.

column2: What happens if Future.result times out before completion?
column3: It raises TimeoutError.

column2: What does Future.exception return for a call that raised an exception?
column3: The exception raised by the call.

column2: What does a false result from set_running_or_notify_cancel indicate?
column3: The Future was cancelled; waiting threads are notified.

column2: Does Queue provide the locking needed for safe exchange between threads?
column3: Yes; the class implements the required locking semantics.

column2: Which kind of queue retrieves the most recently added entry first?
column3: A LIFO queue.

column2: What does a nonpositive maxsize mean for LifoQueue capacity?
column3: Its size is unbounded.

column2: Which priority-queue entries are retrieved first?
column3: The lowest-valued entries.

column2: Does empty() returning false guarantee that the next get will not block?
column3: No.

column2: Does full() returning false guarantee that the next put will not block?
column3: No.

column2: What happens when nonblocking Queue.put finds no free slot?
column3: It raises Full and ignores timeout.

column2: What should a consumer call after finishing a task fetched with get?
column3: Queue.task_done.

column2: Why does immediate queue shutdown require caution when using join?
column3: It can unblock join without work having been done, breaking the usual completion invariant.

column2: What happens to put calls after Queue.shutdown?
column3: They raise ShutDown; blocked put callers are also awakened and raise it.

column2: Why is CPython's SimpleQueue.put appropriate in destructors or weakref callbacks?
column3: Its C implementation is reentrant without deadlocking or corrupting state.

column2: What does a nonblocking SimpleQueue.get do when no item is available?
column3: It raises Empty and ignores timeout.

column2: Which low-level temporary-file helpers require manual cleanup?
column3: mkstemp and mkdtemp.

column2: May portable code rely on TemporaryFile having a visible filesystem name?
column3: No; naming behavior differs across platforms.

column2: Why does TemporaryFile default to binary mode?
column3: To behave consistently across platforms regardless of stored data.

column2: Does delete_on_close affect NamedTemporaryFile when delete=False?
column3: No; it is ignored.

column2: Why can additional open handles cause NamedTemporaryFile cleanup to fail on Windows?
column3: Handles without delete sharing must close before the context exits, or unlink may raise PermissionError.

column2: What causes SpooledTemporaryFile to move its contents to disk?
column3: Exceeding max_size or calling fileno.

column2: What does TemporaryDirectory remove when its context completes?
column3: The directory and all its contents.

column2: How does ignore_cleanup_errors affect TemporaryDirectory cleanup?
column3: It suppresses cleanup errors and deletes removable items on a best-effort basis.

column2: How can TemporaryDirectory retain its tree after context exit for debugging?
column3: Set delete=False.

column2: Does mkstemp automatically insert a dot before its suffix?
column3: No; the caller must include it in the suffix.

column2: Can tempfile.tempdir be a path-like object?
column3: No; it must be bytes or str when set.

column2: Why is generating a name with mktemp before creating the file insecure?
column3: Another process can create that name during the gap; immediate creation avoids the race.

column2: Are IntFlag members also integer instances?
column3: Yes.

column2: Which enum metaclass handles member creation and duplicate values?
column3: EnumType.

column2: What performance penalty can mutable enum values cause during creation?
column3: A quadratic cost relative to the number of mutable or unhashable values.

column2: What happens when _order_ disagrees with the actual enumeration order?
column3: An error is raised.

column2: Does an integer operation preserve an IntEnum member's enumeration status?
column3: No; the resulting value loses that status.

column2: Is the result of a string operation on StrEnum still an enumeration member?
column3: No.

column2: How can a StrEnum member be passed to code requiring exact str type?
column3: Convert it with str(member).

column2: Do bitwise operations on Flag members return members of the enumeration?
column3: Yes; results are members or aliases of members.

column2: What does inversion of an IntFlag return?
column3: A positive union of the flags absent from the operand.

column2: Is an enum's member-creating __new__ still used after all members have been created?
column3: No.

column2: How does auto choose values for Flag and IntFlag?
column3: The first power of two greater than the highest existing value.

column2: Can an enum property and a same-named member be defined in the same class?
column3: No; they must be defined in separate classes.

column2: Does a weak reference by itself keep its referent alive?
column3: No; garbage collection may reclaim it once only weak references remain.

column2: What happens to a WeakValueDictionary entry when its value is garbage collected?
column3: The corresponding mapping entry is deleted.

column2: Who ensures that a registered finalizer stays alive until its target is collected?
column3: The weakref module manages that lifetime automatically.

column2: Are functions written in C among the function objects supporting weak references?
column3: No; Python-written functions are supported, but C functions are excluded from that category.

column2: In what order do multiple weak-reference callbacks for the same object run?
column3: Most recently registered first, then older callbacks.

column2: What happens if a weak reference is hashed for the first time after its referent was deleted?
column3: TypeError is raised.

column2: What does ref.__callback__ return after the referent is no longer alive?
column3: None.

column2: When are entries removed from a WeakKeyDictionary?
column3: When no strong reference to the key remains.

column2: Why must the result of calling an exposed internal weak reference be checked?
column3: The reference may no longer be live.

column2: Can exceptions in finalizer callbacks during garbage collection propagate normally?
column3: No; they are shown on standard error but cannot be propagated.

column2: Why should a finalizer callback not be a bound method of its target object?
column3: That would retain a reference to the target and prevent its collection.

column2: Is finalizer execution guaranteed when created in a daemon thread as the program exits?
column3: No; it may not run at exit.

column2: What does AbstractContextManager's default __enter__ return?
column3: self.

column2: How can a contextmanager-decorated generator support repeated function calls as a decorator?
column3: A new generator instance is created for every call.

column2: For which resource types is contextlib.closing especially useful?
column3: Third-party types with close methods that lack context-manager support.

column2: What does nullcontext return from __enter__?
column3: The supplied enter_result.

column2: How does suppress handle unsuppressed members of a BaseExceptionGroup?
column3: It re-raises them in a new group produced with derive.

column2: Why is contextlib.chdir unsuitable for most threaded or asynchronous code?
column3: It changes the process-wide working directory.

column2: Are ExitStack callbacks invoked automatically when the stack is garbage collected?
column3: No; closing the stack or leaving its with block invokes them.

column2: What does ExitStack.push assume about an object that is not a context manager?
column3: It is a callback with the signature of __exit__.

column2: What is the primary use of ExitStack with a variable number of resources?
column3: Managing a variable number of context managers and cleanup operations in one with statement.

column2: Can ExitStack.callback be used as a decorator to declare cleanup in advance?
column3: Yes.

column2: Does reentrancy imply thread safety for redirect_stdout?
column3: No; it modifies the global sys.stdout binding.

column2: What happens when the same ExitStack is used in nested with statements?
column3: The innermost exit clears the stack.

column2: How can the macOS proxy-discovery problem in programs using fork be avoided?
column3: Set the no_proxy environment variable to '*'.

column2: How is proxy configuration supplied to modern urllib.request instead of the old urlopen dictionary argument?
column3: Using ProxyHandler objects.

column2: Which proxy environment variable wins if uppercase and lowercase forms disagree?
column3: The lowercase form.

column2: What Content-Type is added when Request has data but no Content-Type header?
column3: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

column2: Where does ProxyHandler obtain Windows proxy settings when proxy environment variables are absent?
column3: The registry's Internet Settings section.

column2: What interface should ProxyBasicAuthHandler's password manager support?
column3: The HTTPPasswordMgr interface.

column2: How can a Request constructor override automatic HTTP method selection?
column3: Pass an explicit method argument.

column2: For which protocols does OpenerDirector.open's timeout feature work?
column3: HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP.

column2: Which BaseHandler method should a subclass override for otherwise unhandled HTTP errors?
column3: http_error_default.

column2: How does the default redirect handler handle a POST redirected by a 301 or 302 response?
column3: It follows browser behavior and changes POST to GET.

column2: Can urlretrieve verify download length when no Content-Length header is supplied?
column3: No; it returns the data without checking its size.

column2: Which URLopener method is called for an unrecognized scheme?
column3: open_unknown.

column2: Which higher-level standard-library module uses http.client for HTTP and HTTPS URLs?
column3: urllib.request.

column2: What port does HTTPSConnection use by default?
Does HTTPSConnection perform certificate and hostname checks by default?
column3: Yes.

column2: Where is the file pointer positioned after parse_headers returns?
column3: Ready to read the HTTP body.

column2: What does RemoteDisconnected indicate when getresponse reads no data?
column3: The remote endpoint has closed the connection.

column2: What form should the request URL normally take in HTTPConnection.request?
column3: An absolute path, with documented proxy, OPTIONS, and CONNECT exceptions.

column2: What does encode_chunked=False assume when Transfer-Encoding is already specified?
column3: The calling code handles the encoding.

column2: What should a caller do if the server is not known to support HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer?
column3: Specify Content-Length or supply a string or bytes-like non-file body.

column2: Where does positive HTTPConnection debugging output go?
column3: Standard output.

column2: Does set_tunnel generate the mandatory Host header when none is provided?
column3: Yes, for its HTTP/1.1 CONNECT request.

column2: Why does endheaders ignore empty chunks yielded by an iterator body?
column3: To avoid premature request termination from malformed chunk encoding.

column2: Can an HTTPResponse be used in a with statement?
column3: Yes.

column2: Are Python codecs restricted to converting text to bytes?
column3: No; text-to-text, bytes-to-bytes, and custom arbitrary-type transformations are supported.

column2: Should CodecInfo's encode and decode functions retain state between calls?
column3: No; they are expected to operate statelessly.

column2: Does codecs.open automatically convert newline characters when encoding is specified?
column3: No; the underlying file is opened in binary mode without newline conversion.

column2: Why is rot_13 unsupported by iterdecode?
column3: iterdecode requires bytes input, while rot_13 is text-to-text.

column2: When is a callback registered by register_error invoked?
column3: On an encoding or decoding error when its registered name is selected as the errors parameter.

column2: What does Codec.encode return besides the output object?
column3: The length of input consumed.

column2: Which codec class supports encoding input across multiple steps?
column3: IncrementalEncoder.

column2: Which codec class supports decoding input across multiple steps?
column3: IncrementalDecoder.

column2: May StreamReader.read return more decoded data than requested by chars?
column3: No; it may return less but never more.

column2: Which side of StreamRecoder uses the Reader and Writer components?
column3: The backend, operating on the underlying stream.

column2: Are Python-specific codec names meaningful outside Python?
column3: No; these predefined codec names are specific to Python.

column2: How often does a stateful utf_8_sig encoder write a BOM?
column3: Only once, on the first write.

column2: What familiar configuration-file structure does ConfigParser resemble?
column3: Windows INI files.

column2: Does ConfigParser infer numeric or boolean value types automatically?
column3: No; it stores values as strings.

column2: Are INI section names and option keys equally case sensitive by default?
column3: No; section names are case sensitive and option keys are not.

column2: How does ExtendedInterpolation refer to an option in another section?
column3: With ${section:option} syntax.

column2: What case are option names normally yielded in during section iteration?
column3: Lowercase, after optionxform processing.

column2: Are inline comments enabled by default in ConfigParser?
column3: No; whole-line comment prefixes are '#' and ';'.

column2: What happens to blank lines when empty lines in values are disallowed?
column3: They split keys instead of continuing multiline values.

column2: Which access style is preferred over the legacy get/set API for new projects?
column3: Mapping protocol access.

column2: How can ConfigParser interpolation be disabled entirely?
column3: Pass interpolation=None.

column2: Which section does has_option assume when its section argument is None or empty?
column3: DEFAULT.

column2: How does read_dict handle non-string configuration values?
column3: It automatically converts them to strings.

column2: When does a strict parser raise DuplicateOptionError?
column3: When an option occurs twice while reading a single file, string, or dictionary.

column2: What does doctest do with text resembling interactive Python sessions?
column3: It executes the sessions and checks their shown results.

column2: What does testfile normally display when every example succeeds?
column3: Nothing.

column2: Does doctest expand tabs produced by the tested code itself?
column3: No; source tabs are expanded but generated output tabs are not.

column2: What does NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE change in output comparison?
column3: Any sequence of whitespace can match any other sequence.

column2: How many failing examples can be reported with FAIL_FAST enabled?
column3: At most one; remaining examples are not run.

column2: Can testfile's filename be absolute when module_relative=True?
column3: No; it must be a module-relative path using forward slashes.

column2: What additional test material can testmod find in a module's __test__ mapping?
column3: Functions, classes, and strings whose docstrings or contents hold examples.

column2: What object is passed to DocFileSuite's setUp function?
column3: A DocTest object, with test globals available as globs.

column2: What happens to an example option flag not specified in its options dictionary?
column3: It retains the runner's default setting.

column2: What does DocTestParser.parse return?
column3: A list alternating Example objects and intervening strings.

column2: Which exception does DebugRunner raise when actual output differs from expected output?
column3: DocTestFailure.

column2: Can a doctest example contain both expected output and an exception?
column3: No; that combination is unsupported.

column2: What facility provides pdb command and argument tab completion?
column3: The readline module.

column2: Do assignments made through pdb affect an active optimized scope in Python 3.13?
column3: Yes; they take effect immediately.

column2: What does pdb.runcall return after the invoked function finishes?
column3: The function's own return value.

column2: How can Pdb be prevented from installing its SIGINT handler?
column3: Set nosigint=True.

column2: How are multiple debugger commands separated on one input line?
column3: With a double semicolon.

column2: Which help command describes pdb's exclamation-mark command?
column3: help exec.

column2: What does the clear command do with a filename:lineno argument?
column3: It clears all breakpoints at that line.

column2: What happens when a breakpoint's condition command is given without a condition?
column3: Its existing condition is removed.

column2: What does the silent breakpoint command suppress?
column3: The usual message announcing the breakpoint stop.

column2: In which frame can the jump command change the next executed line?
column3: Only the bottom-most frame.

column2: Do variable assignments in pdb.interact modify the original namespace?
column3: No; it uses a dedicated namespace, although mutations of shared objects still affect them.

column2: How can post-mortem debugging switch between chained exceptions?
column3: Use exceptions to list them and exceptions followed by a number to select one.

column2: Are sys module variables generally writable unless stated otherwise?
column3: No; they are read-only unless explicitly documented otherwise.

column2: Are the number and types of arguments for a sys.audit event a stable API?
column3: Yes; they should not change between releases.

column2: Does sys._current_frames require cooperation from deadlocked threads?
column3: No.

column2: What happens to source-tree __pycache__ directories when pycache_prefix is set?
column3: They are ignored in favor of a parallel cache tree under the prefix.

column2: Can changes to an exception instance be reflected by later exc_info calls while it is handled?
column3: Yes; type and traceback are derived from the instance.

column2: Which C header's constants correspond to sys.float_info fields?
column3: float.h.

column2: Which filename type is recommended for best compatibility?
column3: str, though bytes filenames are supported.

column2: What does _getframemodulename return when the requested depth exceeds the call stack?
column3: None.

column2: Does sys.implementation.version necessarily equal the supported Python language version?
column3: No; it identifies the implementation version, which can differ.

column2: What is platlibdir typically set to on 64-bit Fedora and SuSE?
column3: lib64.

column2: Does stdlib_module_names list submodules such as email.message?
column3: No; only the main package is listed.

column2: Does changing sys.winver change the registry keys used by Python?
column3: No; it is informational only.

column2: When does cached_property run again after caching its value as an attribute?
column3: Only on a lookup when that same-named attribute no longer exists.

column2: Why does cached_property fail on slots-only instances without __dict__?
column3: It needs a mutable instance __dict__ mapping.

column2: What conversion does cmp_to_key perform?
column3: It turns an old-style comparison function into a key function.

column2: What repeated work can lru_cache avoid?
column3: Recomputing expensive or I/O-bound calls with the same arguments.

column2: What does lru_cache(typed=True) do with arguments of different types?
column3: It caches them separately.

column2: Does mutating the dictionary returned by cache_parameters change the cache settings?
column3: No; it is informational only.

column2: Why should functions creating distinct mutable objects not generally be LRU-cached?
column3: The cache reuses previous values rather than producing a new object on each call.

column2: What can improve performance if total_ordering's derived comparisons are a bottleneck?
column3: Implement all six rich comparison methods directly.

column2: What does partial freeze to produce a simplified callable?
column3: Some positional arguments or keyword arguments of a function.

column2: Where is self inserted when partialmethod wraps a non-descriptor callable?
column3: As the first positional argument, before the supplied partial arguments.

column2: Where must singledispatchmethod appear when stacked with classmethod to allow register?
column3: As the outermost decorator.

column2: Which attribute does update_wrapper add to expose the original function?
column3: __wrapped__.

column2: Does shutil.copyfile copy file metadata as well as contents?
column3: No; it copies contents only.

column2: Does copymode change file contents, owner, or group?
column3: No; it copies permission bits only.

column2: What name does shutil.copy use when the destination is a directory?
column3: The source file's base filename.

column2: Does copy2 raise an exception solely because some metadata cannot be preserved?
column3: No; it preserves what the platform permits.

column2: What does copytree do with symbolic links when symlinks=True?
column3: It recreates them as links, preserving their metadata as supported.

column2: What arguments are passed to a custom copytree copy_function?
column3: The source and destination paths.

column2: May rmtree's top-level path be a symbolic link to a directory?
column3: No; it must point to a directory itself.

column2: Does Python 3.13 rmtree ignore FileNotFoundError for a missing top-level path?
column3: No; the exception is ignored only below the top level.

column2: In what units are disk_usage's total, used, and free values returned?
column3: Bytes.

column2: Which Windows environment variable helps shutil.which find commands lacking an extension?
column3: PATHEXT.

column2: Relative to what must make_archive's base_dir be given?
column3: root_dir.

column2: What terminal-size fallback is used by default when querying fails?
column3: 80 columns and 24 lines.

column2: Is the default Mersenne Twister generator suitable for cryptographic purposes?
column3: No; it is deterministic and unsuitable for cryptography.

column2: How can free-threaded programs avoid contention on a shared Random instance?
column3: Use a separate Random instance per thread.

column2: Where should the state argument for random.setstate come from?
column3: A prior call to getstate.

column2: Why can supplying cum_weights to choices save work?
column3: It avoids converting relative weights to cumulative weights.

column2: What happens when every weight passed to choices is zero?
column3: ValueError is raised.

column2: Can every permutation of an arbitrarily long sequence be generated by Mersenne Twister?
column3: No; the permutation count can exceed the generator's period.

column2: How can sample represent repeated population elements without expanding them explicitly?
column3: Use its counts keyword argument.

column2: How is expovariate's lambd related to the desired mean?
column3: It is the reciprocal of the mean and must be nonzero.

column2: Can simultaneous gauss calls from two threads produce the same value?
column3: Yes; use separate generators, locks, or normalvariate to avoid that issue.

column2: What distribution does vonmisesvariate produce when kappa is zero?
column3: A uniform random angle from zero to two pi.

column2: Does calling SystemRandom.seed make its sequence reproducible?
column3: No; seed is ignored and sequences are not reproducible.

column2: Can random() produce every representable float between zero and one?
column3: No; it returns only evenly spaced multiples of two to the power minus 53.
